doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Nephew's jazz education, Max Roach, and artists' support in Sweden and Canada
summary: Her nephew studied at Manhattan School of Music and with Max Roach and Milt Hinton, now lives in Sweden, and she considers emigrating to Canada.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. But I know that like my nephew went to school, the Manhattan School of Music, studying jazz. But even before that when he was a kid he went to jazz camp and his counselor was — oh dear, great drummer —
No. His daughter plays violin. He’s one of my favorite drummers.
Max Roach, yeah. It was his counselor.

And he also studied with Milt Hinton and, you know, these guys. And they give so much to the students. As long as the students are really interested. But yeah, I don’t know, I guess I know I’m lucky. And that’s one nice thing about that Kenji lives in Sweden and they really support the arts there and they really support the artists there. And I think he’s going to be teaching but he’s going to be teaching because he wants to. And he plays whenever he wants and he has healthcare, and they give a stipend to artists. Well there are other countries, I mean Canada, I’ve thought about emigrating to Canada for a number of reasons. But they have very strict rules about who can emigrate. You have to have money, you have to be young, you have to be healthy, you have to know French, you know, all these different criteria which George, with George a couple of years ago I might have managed. But now, you know we’re even older and he’s had problems and we all have problems. But then I found out from unfortunately somebody who’s no longer with us but if you’re an artist, you’re in.
They consider you valuable, you’re in.
